meta.method: Independent read-only openpyxl import and Decimal aggregation; canonical IDs; verified export copies removed; no website values used.
meta.scope: Fictional Lone Mesa Energy, all six sites; Arroyo focus
meta.source_classification: All data is fictional case material. spare_fill_pct and Solutions reductions/costs are provided scenario planning assumptions; event rows are fictional historical system records.

hse_records.control_gap: Review closed gauging and exposure controls

interpretation: Arroyo has the largest aggregate parts-wait burden and highest affected-event frequency, but mean delay per affected event is almost identical to the pooled other-five mean.
Other-five site mean is an unweighted average of five site totals or site percentages; pooled event mean is total wait divided by affected events.
Source fill percentages cannot be pooled into a true company fill rate because requested-part denominators are missing.
Parts waiting is Arroyo largest individual stage; detection plus dispatch combined is larger but comprises two stages.
Asset/cause group wait identifies where to investigate, not which SKU to order.
Cause and stage totals describe overlapping views of the same events, so never add them.
Monthly trend is descriptive of 2025, not a seasonal forecast or live feed.
spare_fill_pct is a provided scenario planning assumption (Dictionary row14), not measured service performance or a probability that a specific SKU is in stock.
Association between low source fill and waiting is descriptive; no causal estimate proves that low fill caused all observed waiting.

O4_scenario.label: Source O4 base case, full implementation on historical 2025 baseline; modeled, not achieved

source_option.prerequisite: Inventory audit included; annual replenishment included
source_option.benefit_rule: Parts waiting stage; all unplanned causes

O4_scenario.contribution_formula: SUM(eligible event parts_wait_hours * O4 reduction * matched asset capacity * (1 - event recoverable_fraction) * (matched asset-month price - variable cost))
limitations: No source O4 dependency on O2, O3, O6, cleanup option, or edge buffering. Inventory audit and annual replenishment included in O4.
Source lead time is 1 month from approval to commissioning; no verified HSE closure dates for open actions, so actual first-year benefit is not determinable.
All detect, dispatch, repair, protected repair and restart hours are unchanged by O4.
Critical HSE costs are a subset of all-open HSE costs; do not add both subtotals.
No source prediction that local fill reaches 100%, that all affected events vanish, or that spending drops by 60%.
No actual SKU, stock balance, order or supplier data is available; auto-order rules must be a labeled proposed workflow.

source_readme.text: Fictional Lone Mesa Energy. 2025 full year; 6 sites; 18 independent affected oil streams. No gas sales modeled.
Assets: asset_id. Events: event_id. Production: asset_id + month. Readings: reading_id. Solutions: option_id. HSE: hse_id. Normalize IDs and remove verified export copies first.

Site fields repeat on three Assets rows. Read staffing, site costs and available project hours once per site. Use these estimates to explain resources and training; identify any additional help and its assumed cost.

Select one primary improvement and include any required supporting options. Use its eligible causes and base stage-reduction fractions to estimate annual avoided hours; low/high fractions are optional reference values.

remaining repair=protected_repair_hours+(repair_hours-protected_repair_hours)*product(1-reductions). Other stages: original*product(1-reductions). Protected time is already inside repair, never additional downtime. No proposed reduction can remove required safety controls.
O1: O2 once/org; O6 + cleanup/site; edge below 97% network uptime. O3: O6 + cleanup/site. O5 pumps only, +6 planned outage hours per treated asset in year one. Pay shared prerequisites once.

Use lead_months for a practical twelve-month roadmap. Annual avoided hours describe full implementation; explain that first-year results may be lower. Training effort = technicians × training_hours_per_person, once per site.

Open actions with potential_severity=5 block the affected site pilot until the site HSE supervisor verifies closure. Include relevant scoped HSE actions, costs and hours; recommendations cannot bypass safety controls.

Use overdue critical action count, verified closure, repeated hazard observations, and spilled minus recovered volume. Severity and likelihood are ordinal scenario bands (1 low, 5 high), not probabilities or legal thresholds. No exposure denominator: do not report injury rates or claim incident prevention from these records.
